state.player: older adult with a diagnosis of early-stage dementia (mild), motivated, supported by an adult-child family member
state.evidence: cognitive training shows small-moderate benefit in mild cognitive impairment; early-stage dementia benefits more from cognitive stimulation (familiarity, reminiscence, errorless/low-failure) than from speed drills
state.app: warm bilingual cognitive mini-games, offline-first, no-fail design, non-clinical
state.regulatory: marketing must stay 'fun mental exercise'; no treatment or prevention claims

primary_audience.instructions: Which population should v1 primarily serve, given the actual player has early-stage dementia?

design_shift.instructions: For an early-dementia player, should the design emphasize errorless, low-failure, familiarity/reminiscence mechanics over speed and adaptive-difficulty drills?

criteria.true: Familiarity and low failure serve this population best
criteria.false: Speed and adaptive difficulty remain more valuable

familiar_content.instructions: Would personalized or familiar content (family photos, familiar objects) meaningfully improve engagement over generic emoji categories for early dementia?

criteria.true: Familiar content drives engagement and meaning
